name: PLC vs TPC Benchmark
description: The convergence of energy transmission and data communication has become a key feature of decentralized energy systems across a broad spectrum of voltage/power ranges, including smart grid applications and cyber-physical power systems. This paper compares two distinct approaches: Power Line Communications (PLC) and Talkative Power Conversion (TPC). While PLC leverages existing power infrastructure for data transmission by using external data transmitters and receivers, TPC integrates communication capabilities directly into power electronic converters. We present their technical foundations and applications, benchmark their strengths and bottlenecks, and outline future research directions regarding TPC that could bridge the gap between power and communication technologies.
evaluation_method: throughput/latency/BER (domain-specific technical metrics) and qualitative comparative analysis
reputation: Niche academic benchmark for comparing PLC and TPC approaches with limited adoption beyond the power-systems research community.
notes: Not an ML benchmark—results depend heavily on hardware, deployment conditions, and simulation assumptions; reproducibility may be limited without detailed experimental configs.
